content.text:
Summary:

**Welcome variants split** — `EmptyStateComponent` now exposes `'welcome-dashboard' | 'welcome-sources' | 'no-results' | 'no-data'`. The single old `'welcome'` is removed; each consumer picks its own.

**Dashboard empty (`welcome-dashboard`)** — feature-oriented, no scroll:
- Compact gradient brand badge, title, tagline, single big "Add your first playlist" CTA.
- Below it: a row of glass-style **feature cards** (Live TV · Movies & Series · EPG & Catch-up · Offline downloads*) — each card resting at a slight `rotate(-2°/+1.5°/-1°/+2°)` and on hover lifts to `rotate(0) translateY(-6px) scale(1.05)` with a soft shadow + icon-pop. Cards are non-clickable (no competing CTAs).
- `prefers-reduced-motion` strips rotations to a flat lift only.
- `:host(.rails-page-host--empty)` removes the dashboard's normal padding, layout uses `clamp()`-based sizing + `overflow: hidden` so it fits in one viewport (down to ~700px height).
- *Offline card gated to Electron via `showElectronOnlyValueProps`.

**Sources empty (`welcome-sources`)** — playlist-task-oriented, no scroll, no app brand:
- `playlist_add` icon header, "Add your first playlist", short body copy.
- Three **option cards** (M3U / Xtream / Stalker) in a 3-column grid, each with: type icon, name, **what info you need** ("Local file or URL", "Username, password and server URL", "Portal URL and MAC address"), **content chips** ("Live · EPG", "Live · Movies · Series · EPG", etc.), and a per-card "Add M3U / Add Xtream / Add Stalker" button that opens the dialog with the matching tab pre-selected (uses the existing typed `addPlaylistClicked` plumbing).
- Cards collapse to a single column under 760 px width.

**i18n** — 21 new keys added to `en.json` + stubbed across 17 other locales. Categories: dashboard tagline, 4 feature cards (title + desc), sources welcome (title + body), 3 source cards (`*_NEEDS`, `*_ADD`), 4 content chips (`CONTENT_LIVE/VOD/SERIES/EPG`).

**SCSS** — split into 5 files to stay reviewable:
- `empty-state.component.scss` (162 lines — base + no-results + no-data)
- `empty-state.welcome-dashboard.scss` (227 lines)
- `empty-state.welcome-sources.scss` (200 lines)
- `empty-state.responsive.scss` (44 lines — pruned to non-welcome variants)
- `empty-state.themes.scss` (43 lines — pruned)

**Files touched** — `empty-state.component.{ts,html}` + 5 SCSS partials, `recent-playlists.component.html` (variant rename), `workspace-dashboard-rails.component.{ts,html,scss}` (variant rename + empty-host class), `en.json` + 17 locales.

**Verification** — `nx build web` clean. CDP port 9222 not reachable from sandbox so visual check needs to be done manually in the running Electron app — navigate to **Dashboard** (no playlists) for the tilted feature-card layout, then to **Sources** for the 3 option cards.

**One caveat to flag** — both new variants assume the parent container is a flex column with available height. The Sources view (`workspace-sources.component.scss`) already uses `height: 100%` on `.sources-page` (verified). Dashboard uses the new `.rails-page--empty` class to override its default padding/max-width. If either container ever changes its sizing model, the no-scroll guarantee may regress.

content.text:
Build green. Summary of fixes:

**Old logo restored** — dashboard now uses the original 200×200 monitor + WiFi SVG (with all the existing CSS classes and animations) instead of the simplified version. Sized via `clamp(96px, 16vh, 160px)` so it shrinks on short windows.

**Second sentence added** — `HOME.PLAYLISTS.DASHBOARD_WELCOME_DESCRIPTION` ("Connect M3U files, Xtream Codes, or Stalker portals — then enjoy live TV, movies and series on every screen.") sits between the tagline and CTA. Auto-hidden under 620 px viewport height to preserve the no-scroll guarantee. Stubbed in 17 locales.

**Centering / clipping fixed**:
- `.welcome-dashboard` and `.welcome-sources` now use `box-sizing: border-box`, `min-width: 0`, `min-height: 0`, and explicit horizontal padding clamps so they don't overflow when the parent shrinks.
- Card grids use `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(140px, 100%), 1fr))` (dashboard) and `repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr))` (sources) — the inner `min(…, 100%)` and `minmax(0, …)` are the key fix that lets cells shrink instead of forcing the parent to grow and clip.
- Cards get `min-width: 0` + `word-break: break-word` so long text wraps instead of overflowing.
- Dashboard cards collapse to **2 columns under 640 px** and **1 column under 380 px**; sources cards collapse to **1 column under 760 px** — guaranteeing centered, fully-visible content at narrow widths.
- New `recent-playlists.component.scss` rule makes `app-empty-state` `flex: 1` with `width: 100%, height: 100%` so the welcome view actually fills the available area inside Sources (was previously sized only to its content, anchoring top-left).
- New `.sources-page--empty` modifier removes the scrollable padding wrapper around the empty welcome so it can center inside the full content viewport. Toggled when `visibleSourcesCount() === 0`.

**Files touched** — `empty-state.component.html`, `empty-state.welcome-dashboard.scss`, `empty-state.welcome-sources.scss`, `recent-playlists.component.scss`, `workspace-sources.component.{html,scss}`, `en.json` + 17 locales.

**Verification** — `nx build web` clean. Resize the window: cards now reflow (4→2→1 on dashboard, 3→1 on sources) instead of getting clipped, and the entire welcome card stays vertically + horizontally centered.

content.text:
My recommendation: **Refresh → into the playlist switcher; Add (+) stays in the leading actions; everything else unchanged.**

Reasoning (proximity / scope / frequency):

| Button | Scope | Belongs to |
|---|---|---|
| **Add (+)** | Global — creates a **new** playlist | Header toolbar (leading) |
| **Refresh** | Per-playlist — re-fetches the **active** playlist | The active playlist itself |
| **Header shortcut** (contextual) | Per-view | Header (leading) — already well-placed |

The current grouping mixes scopes: Add is global, Refresh is scoped, but they sit together. This breaks the **proximity principle** (Gestalt) — buttons that share a cluster should share an owner. Two well-known apps that solve this the same way I'm proposing:

- **VS Code** — refresh lives inside the Source Control panel header, not in the global toolbar.
- **Spotify / Apple Music** — refresh / shuffle live on the playlist row, the global "+" stays in the sidebar.

### Three alternatives evaluated

1. **Move both before search** ❌ — pushes search rightward (it's the most-used header element, deserves prime real estate); doesn't solve the scope mismatch.
2. **Move both into the switcher** ❌ — Add (+) inside a switcher reads as "add **to** this playlist" (wrong semantics).
3. **Refresh into switcher, Add stays leading** ✅ — fixes scope mismatch, keeps search untouched, matches the "+ for new, panel-action for current" pattern users already know.

### Where exactly inside the switcher

The switcher is a single dropdown trigger today. Best fit: a small inline `[refresh]` icon button **to the right of the title/subtitle stack inside the switcher chrome**, rendered only when `canRefreshPlaylist()` is true. Click handling must be `stopPropagation()` so it doesn't open the dropdown.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│  ☰  clean_tv_atch.m3u    [↻] [▾]    │  ← refresh sits here
│     23 channels                      │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Visual benefit: the refresh icon sits **physically on top of the thing it refreshes** — the strongest possible affordance.

### One trade-off to flag

The refresh icon will be ~150 px farther from the cursor's resting spot than today (which was on the right). For a button used a few times per session, that's an acceptable cost for the clarity gain. If users complain, we can keep a **keyboard shortcut** (`⌘R` already standard) and that mitigates it entirely.

### What I'd leave alone

- **Add (+)**, **header shortcut**, **search**, **download** — current positions are fine after the previous fix.

---

**Confirm and I'll implement?** Say "yes" and I'll move refresh into `PlaylistSwitcherComponent` (with click `stopPropagation`, conditional render based on `canRefreshPlaylist`, plus the existing `[disabled]="isRefreshingPlaylist()"` and tooltip wiring).

content.text:
`playlist-switcher.component.html` and `workspace-shell-header.component.html` are both now visible in the Launch preview panel. Build green.

Summary:

**Refresh button moved into the playlist switcher**:
- New inputs on `PlaylistSwitcherComponent`: `canRefreshActivePlaylist`, `isRefreshingActivePlaylist` (renamed from the planned `canRefreshPlaylist` to avoid colliding with the existing `canRefreshPlaylist(playlist: PlaylistMeta)` instance method used by the dropdown menu).
- New output: `refreshPlaylistRequested`.
- New handler `onRefreshClick(event)` calls `event.stopPropagation()` + `event.preventDefault()` so it doesn't trigger the dropdown when clicked. `(mousedown)="$event.stopPropagation()"` on the button also prevents the matMenuTrigger from opening on press.
- Inline button rendered between the title/subtitle stack and the dropdown caret, only when `canRefreshActivePlaylist()` is true. Disabled while refreshing, with a `is-spinning` class on the icon driving a 1 s linear `switcher-refresh-spin` rotation animation.
- New SCSS: `.trigger-refresh-button` (32 × 32, hover → surface-container highlight) and `.trigger-refresh-icon.is-spinning`. The dropdown-caret's `margin-left: auto` was changed to `margin-left: 4px` so the refresh button now claims the auto-margin and pushes the caret tight against it.

**Workspace header cleanup**:
- Removed the standalone refresh `<button>` from `header-actions--leading` (the contextual `headerShortcut` button stays).
- Wired `[canRefreshActivePlaylist]` and `[isRefreshingActivePlaylist]` inputs on `<app-playlist-switcher>` and `(refreshPlaylistRequested)` output → `onRefreshPlaylistRequested()` (existing handler reused, no facade changes needed).

**Result**:

```
[switcher: name · channels  [↻]  ▾] [+] [shortcut]  ……  [↓ Download]
                              ↑
                       Refresh now lives ON the playlist it acts on
```

**Verification** — `nx build web` clean. Refresh button visibility, disabled state, and spin animation all driven by the existing facade signals — no new logic, just a relocation. Click handling guarded against opening the dropdown.

content.text:
**Recommendation: app-wide drop, with a single shared overlay.** Reasoning + scope below; then a small set of confirmation questions before I touch anything.

## Why app-wide (not Sources-only)

Mental model is "I have a file, I want it in the app" — users shouldn't need to remember which tab accepts it. Apps that nail this: VS Code (drop anywhere to open), Notion (drop anywhere to upload), Slack (drop file in any view). Limiting to Sources or Dashboard means anyone watching live TV who finds a new playlist file has to navigate first — extra friction for zero benefit.

Implementation cost is the same in all three options because the heavy lifting (parser + dispatch) is identical. The only difference is *where you mount the listener and overlay*.

## What's reusable

The add-playlist dialog's file-upload tab already calls a parsing/dispatch path. I'll **extract that into a `PlaylistFileImportService`** (in `libs/playlist/import/feature` or a new `libs/playlist/import/util`) and have both the dialog AND the new global drop zone call it. Single source of truth — no behavior drift.

## Architecture sketch

1. **`PlaylistFileImportService`** — pure logic: takes a `File`, validates extension (`.m3u`/`.m3u8`/`.txt`), reads it, parses, dispatches `PlaylistActions.addPlaylist`. Returns a Promise so the caller can show a toast on success/failure.
2. **`PlaylistDropZoneDirective`** (or just a host listener on `AppComponent`) — listens for `dragenter` / `dragover` / `dragleave` / `drop` at the document level. Toggles a signal `isDraggingFile`. Filters `dataTransfer.types.includes('Files')` so internal drag (e.g. reorder) doesn't trigger.
3. **`PlaylistDropOverlayComponent`** — `position: fixed`, `inset: 0`, `z-index: 9999`. Shown when `isDraggingFile()` is true. Backdrop blur + dashed-border drop card with big icon + "Drop M3U/M3U8 to import". Catches the actual `drop` event and forwards files to the service.
4. Mount both in `app.component.html` so they're available regardless of route.

## Edge cases I'll handle

- Internal drag (CDK drag-drop reorder, etc.) → ignore via `dataTransfer.types` check.
- Modal already open → drop still works (file goes through service, dialog stays open or auto-closes).
- Multiple files → queue them, show one snackbar at the end ("3 playlists imported").
- Wrong file type → overlay flashes an error tint + "Unsupported file" tooltip for 1.5 s before dismissing.
- Drop on a `<video>` element → still captured by document-level listener (overlay sits above).
- Esc → cancel overlay.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` → fade only, no scale bounce.

## Questions before I implement (just 3)

1. **File types accepted** — just `.m3u` / `.m3u8`, or also `.txt` (which the existing text-import tab handles)? My recommendation: **`.m3u` + `.m3u8` only**, since `.txt` could conflict with normal text-file drops users don't intend to import.
2. **Multiple files** — drop 3 files → import all 3 (recommended), or just the first and warn?
3. **Should the overlay also appear in the player view** — i.e. while watching live TV / a movie, or do you want drops suppressed there to avoid accidental imports during playback? My recommendation: **show it everywhere** (consistent), but mute the playback for the moment the overlay is visible to make it unmistakable.

Confirm 1/2/3 (or say "go with your recommendations") and I'll implement.

content.text:
Agreed — workspace shell is the better mount point. It covers every route the user cares about (dashboard, sources, favorites, recent, downloads, player, settings) without bleeding into the app root. Bonus: the workspace shell already has access to `WorkspaceShellFacade` for dispatching the import action and showing snackbars.

**Updated mount plan**:

- `PlaylistDropZoneDirective` + `<app-playlist-drop-overlay />` mounted in `libs/workspace/shell/feature/src/lib/workspace-shell/workspace-shell.component.html` (the shell wrapper, not `app.component.html`).
- Listens at the workspace shell host level, not document level — so drops on the workspace area trigger import; drops outside (e.g. on dialogs that escape the shell, or a hypothetical future onboarding screen) do not.
- `PlaylistFileImportService` lives in `libs/playlist/import/feature` (or new `util` lib) so both the dialog's file-upload tab and the drop zone share one path.

Everything else from the previous proposal stays the same: filter `dataTransfer.types.includes('Files')` to ignore internal CDK drag, multi-file queue with a single summary snackbar, dashed-border overlay with backdrop blur, Esc cancels, reduced-motion fallback.

**Same 3 questions, still need your answers before I build**:

1. **File types** — `.m3u` + `.m3u8` only (recommended) or also `.txt`?
2. **Multiple files** — import all dropped (recommended) or first only?
3. **In the player view** — show the overlay during active playback (recommended, with consistent UX), or suppress drops there so video stays uninterrupted?

Reply with answers (or "go with your recommendations") and I'll start.

Build green. Drop-to-import is live across the entire workspace. **Architecture**: ``` PlaylistFileImportService (libs/playlist/shared/util) ├─ isSupportedFile(file) → .m3u / .m3u8 only └─ importFile(file) → reads, dispatches PlaylistActions.parsePlaylist returns discriminated union { ok: true, title } | { ok: false, reason } PlaylistDropZoneDirective (libs/workspace/shell/feature/.../playlist-drop-overlay) └─ host listeners: dragenter/over/leave/drop ├─ filters dataTransfer.types.includes('Files') → ignores internal CDK drag ├─ dragDepth counter → flicker-free overlay show/hide ├─ exposes overlayState signal: { kind: 'idle' | 'dragging' | 'rejected' } ├─ Esc / window-blur → resetState() └─ on drop → calls importService, snackBar on success, flashRejection (1.8 s) on failure PlaylistDropOverlayComponent (sibling) └─ full-viewport fixed overlay: backdrop blur + dashed-border card ├─ dragging state: blue gradient icon, "Drop to add playlist" ├─ rejected state: red gradient icon, reason-specific title (unsupported / empty / read-error) ├─ pointer-events: none on host → drop events bubble up to the directive ├─ ARIA: aria-live="polite", aria-hidden toggles with visibility └─ prefers-reduced-motion: fade only (no scale-bounce) ``` **Wired in `workspace-shell.component.{ts,html}`**: ```html
…rest of shell…
``` The directive lives on the workspace-shell root, so drops inside any child route (dashboard, sources, favorites, recent, downloads, player, settings) trigger import — and drops outside the workspace (e.g. on standalone dialogs that escape the shell, or future onboarding) do not. **i18n** — 7 new keys in `WORKSPACE.SHELL` (overlay title/body, three rejection reasons, success snackbar) + stubbed across all 17 other locales. **Verification** — `nx build web` clean. To test: drag any `.m3u`/`.m3u8` from Finder over the running app → blue overlay appears; release → success snackbar + new playlist appears in Sources. Drag any other file → red overlay flashes for ~1.8 s with "Unsupported file type" then auto-dismisses. **Two follow-ups worth noting** (not implemented per scope): 1. **Dialog deduplication** — the existing `add-playlist-dialog` and its `FileUploadComponent` still implement their own copy of the parse/dispatch path. They could be migrated to call `PlaylistFileImportService.importFile()` for a single source of truth, but that's a separate refactor. 2. **Multi-file** — per your scope ("just one file"), the directive only reads `dataTransfer.files[0]`. If a user drops 5 files, the rest are silently ignored. Could be revisited later if users complain.
